new_public_PR_reads.title: Lay a click-lock vinyl floor tile: angle its tongue into the laid row's groove, then lower it flat to lock by AMMistry18 · Pull Request #1920 · robocurve/benchmark-tasks · GitHub
comments: The robot lays a real-size rigid-core click-lock vinyl floor tile (600 x 300 mm, 1.55 kg) against a row already laid, using the angle-in method carpenters and floor layers use on floating floors. The two arms work the tile's near half together: they keep the long tongue angled up into the laid row's groove along its whole length, slide the tile's end against the 10 mm wall spacer, and lower it flat so the joint hooks shut. A tile lowered before its tongue is home rides on the groove's locking bump with an open seam about 1.4 mm high, and it scores 0. Scoring measures the seam, lippage and end gap with a feeler gauge, straightedge and ruler, and needs the tile released and at rest. task.json : instruction, setup, scoring, run limit, fidelity and scores README.md : run and score commands, the tile, profile, laid row, wall, spacer and batten dimensions, scoring, the scripted demo, real-trial checks and licences lay_click_lock_vinyl_tile.py : scene (tile and laid row with the click profile as contact geometry), scorer and scripted demo yam_parts.py , yam_joints.py , yam_mesh.py : kit modules, copied unchanged test_lay_click_lock_vinyl_tile.py : offline checks of the scorer on goal, partial-credit and cheat layouts, and of the demo's reach 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

new_public_PR_reads.title: Caliper measure by Jingyi-Z · Pull Request #601 · robocurve/benchmark-tasks · GitHub
comments: Measure a pin's diameter with a digital caliper, holding it in the jaws Category: Impact on jobs Run limit: 1,200 steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz) Task: Measure the diameter of the aluminium pin with the digital caliper. Pick the pin up with one hand and hold it upright between the caliper's open jaws, square to them and close to the fixed jaw (the jaw at the caliper's left end). Keep holding it, but loosely, so it can slide across the jaws: there is nothing under the jaws, so a pin let go falls. With the other hand, push the black thumb rest at the slider's right end to the left to close the sliding jaw until it has carried the pin against the fixed jaw and both jaws just touch it. Do not squeeze: pressing on the jaw makes the display read low. Then take that hand off the slider and keep the pin still between the jaws, so the display shows its diameter. Description: Checking a part's size with a caliper is a routine step in machining, inspection and lab work. A part held cocked or stiffly off the fixed jaw, or a heavy thumb on the slider, gives a wrong reading, so one hand holds the part square but loosely while the other closes the jaw gently and lets it seat the part on the fixed jaw. Scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (it moved both hands around the caliper but never picked up the pin), demo: 1.0 (one hand held the pin loosely between the jaws while the other closed the slider, which carried the pin onto the fixed jaw; the display then read its diameter with the slider let go) Setup Dream-1 run Scripted demo Top camera, 20 Hz. Run commands, scoring and assets: README .
